questions.q: What is a bank deposit in the context of modern money?
questions.a: A bank deposit is money safely kept in a bank account that can be withdrawn or transferred on demand. If a student thinks a bank deposit is just a physical piggy bank hidden at home, they misunderstand that modern money exists as electronic or ledger records managed by regulated financial institutions.

questions.q: Why is a cheque considered a modern form of money even though it is just a piece of paper?
questions.a: A cheque is an instruction to a bank to transfer a specific sum of money from the drawer's account to the payee's account, acting as a substitute for physical cash in large transactions. A wrong answer stating that a cheque is actual currency reveals the misconception that the paper itself has intrinsic value, rather than serving as an order to move funds recorded in bank deposits.

questions.q: Rohan has ₹10,000 in his savings account. He writes a cheque of ₹3,500 to buy books. If his initial bank balance is ₹10,000, what is his new bank balance after the cheque is cleared?
questions.a: Steps: 1) Identify initial bank deposit = ₹10,000. 2) Identify the amount withdrawn or transferred via cheque = ₹3,500. 3) Subtract the cheque amount from the initial deposit: ₹10,000 - ₹3,500 = ₹6,500. 4) The new bank deposit balance is ₹6,500. A wrong answer like ₹13,500 shows the student incorrectly added the transaction amount instead of subtracting a payment.

questions.q: How do digital money transfers (like UPI) differ from writing a traditional paper cheque?
questions.a: Digital transfers execute instantly through electronic networks communicating directly between bank servers 24/7, whereas cheques require physical clearance through a clearing house taking 1-3 working days. A wrong answer claiming they are identical ignores the speed and technological infrastructure differences that accelerate modern market trade.

questions.q: Evaluate why a merchant in a busy market would prefer digital payments over cash transactions at the end of the day.

Digital payments reduce the risk of theft, eliminate the need to carry heavy cash to the bank, provide automatic digital accounting records, and save time spent counting change. A student who argues cash is always superior overlooks the safety, efficiency, and transaction-tracking benefits that modern digital infrastructure provides to businesses.
